recipes.name: Citrus Chicken Stir Fry
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, cut into thin strips
1 (16 ounce) bag frozen stir-fry vegetables, thawed

steps.text: Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil.
Stir in whole-wheat noodles and return to a boil. Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the pasta has cooked through but is firm to the bite, 5 to 8 minutes. Drain well and set aside.
Combine chicken stock, orange marmalade, tamari sauce, whole ginger root piece, and ground black pepper in a pot over medium-high heat.
Bring sauce to a boil and reduce heat to medium. Simmer until sauce reduces and thickens; about 20 minutes.
Remove sauce from heat. Stir in lemon juice and set aside.
Heat peanut oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook and stir chicken in hot oil until golden, no longer pink in the center, and the juices run clear, 5 to 10 minutes.
Remove chicken from skillet and set aside, leaving oil in the pan.
Cook and stir the stir-fry vegetables in the same skillet used for the chicken until vegetables are almost tender, 4 to 5 minutes.
Remove ginger root piece from sauce and discard.
Stir chicken and sauce into vegetables and cook until heated through, 1 to 2 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Citrus Chicken Stir Fry
raw_recipe.description: This quick and easy citrus chicken stir fry gets its kick from a combination of flavors including lemon juice, fresh ginger, and orange marmalade.

review.reviewBody: This was amazing thank you! The sauce was the best. I used fresh vegetables and did not have the noodles so served with basmati rice.

This is a keeper! Very tasty! Usually my husband adds soy sauce or Texas Pete to my stir-fry meals but he didn't add anything to this! What I did: sauteed 1 clove of chopped garlic in olive oil & butter, added 2 chicken breasts (sliced in thin strips) and cooked until no pink showed. Pushed chicken to outer edges of pan and added onion, carrot, celery, mushrooms, and red pepper to center of pan (what was on hand). Topped with 1 1/2 tablespoons of soy sauce, 2 tablespoons of OJ concentrate, 1/4 tsp. ground ginger, salt & fresh ground pepper. Covered & cooked until vegis done, stirring occasionally. Juiced 1/4 lemon and sprinkled over all. Stirred and served over wheat noodles. Will try rice next time. Thanks for a great recipe!
Had many complements! I seasoned the chicken before cooking with garlic, fresh ginger a little orange juice, soy sauce and herbs. Will definitely make it again!

Love this recipe. I like other reviewers used soy sauce instead of tamari. Added garlic to the chicken and fresh vegetables. Did not discard the ginger.Served with our favorite basmati rice recipe from this site. Note: Double the sauce: its that good!

This turned out well with adaptations for what I had. Used Apricot jam (did not have orange marmalade). Used Ponzu sauce instead of Tamari (to add citrus). Used ready to stir fry Asian noodles. Had sliced mushrooms and frozen pea pods. Added chopped onions and garlic and cooked these together rather than the stir fry veggies. Might marinade the chicken next time with orange juice and soy sauce before cooking it.

Pretty good, though doesn't have much flavor as written. We added seasoning (a citrus & basil rub blend I had) to the chicken while it was cooking, as well as some crushed red pepper flakes to the sauce. I didn't cook the pasta, but served the stir fry over rice instead.

This was very good! The flavors of the orange marmalade and tamari sauce really made this dish. I agree with the other reviewers I also left the ginger in. I used Basmati rice with a mixture of broccoli, cauliflower, carrots, green onion and some pineapple. Fabulous!

For the first time, I followed this recipe to the letter. I doubled the sauce recipe as it didn't sound like enough. Glad I did I also thickened the sauce with flour and water, as I couldn't find the cornstarch and I prefer the sauce a little thicker and it was still a little runny after simmering for 20-25 minutes. I too, used lite soy sauce because it was what I had on hand. My husband said it was as good as any restaurant entrée! Oh yeah, I served over rice instead of pasta. Delish!
This was easy enough. I thought this would be better over rice as another suggested. My noodles got soggy. I did like the sauce it was simple but good. I also subbed soy sauce for the tamari
I really lived the citrus flavor. I used udon noodles, and regular soy sauce. Next time I will use sugar free marmalade to cut downnon calories
I reversed the order of cooking. I made the sauce first and while it was reducing, I cooked the noodles. The chicken only took 2 to 3 minutes to cook. It was very good.
Easy and great tasting MIld enough for entire family. Lots of pots but whatever

Made a really nice change from 'chicken'. I love chicken but I end up cooking it pretty much the same way all of the time. Not any more!! This was very tasty and easy to put together although I took quite a bit longer to do so. All around - great recipe.
I loved this dish and will definitely make it again! The sauce has just the right amount of tartness. The only thing I didn't like is how many pans it took
Followed recipe except added extra water chestnuts and mushrooms and served over egg noodles, (that’s what we had). Turned out really good!!!

It was very good. Good recipe with very good tasting sauce. I think it would be better with Brown Rice substituting for the noodles. The noodle were good but my ptrference would be rice. My sauce did not thicken as the recipe indicated it would but very tasty.
The sauce is amazing. It is easier to make than my usual recipe, and is also tastier. Hubs raved about it. I will make it often. Thanks for sharing.
It was a hit! Minor detail: I used regular soy instead of tamari.
This was very good, I used fresh vegetables. I will make again.
Big hit with my super picky, anti-vegetable family. They pick out the veggies and give them to me! It's a win, win.
